title: Can a string be split into dictionary words?
summary: Mark every position of a long string where a clean cut can be made, and check whether the end gets a mark.
goal: Decide whether the whole string splits into dictionary words

mapping.story: A clean cut before position i

examples.label: catsandog
examples.explanation: Every split leaves og or sandog unmatched.

examples.label: cars
examples.explanation: ca + rs works, even though car leaves s.

ladder.name: Try every split
ladder.idea: Try every dictionary word at the start; for each that fits, recursively split the rest.

ladder.name: Mark every reachable cut
ladder.idea: Mark position 0. For each marked position, mark every position reachable by one dictionary word from it. The answer is whether the end is marked.
ladder.insight: Whether the rest of the string can be split depends only on where it starts, not on how we got there. Marking each position once replaces exploring every split.

transfer.problem: Can a long URL without separators, such as findmeaparking, be split into English words?
transfer.explanation: Mark every position reachable by a dictionary word from an earlier marked position, starting at 0.

selfCheck: Only extends from positions already marked.
Uses a set for fast word lookups.
Returns whether the last position is marked.
